facts.note: The whistles that were first adopted by referees were made by Joseph Hudson at Mills Munitions in Birmingham, England.
Hudson demonstrated his whistle to Scotland Yard and was awarded his first contract in 1884.
The whistle was not mentioned in the Laws of the Game until 1936
Before the introduction of the whistle, referees indicated their decisions by waving a white handkerchief.

facts.note: Initially there existed two umpires, one per team, who could be appealed to with the referee (the game's timekeeper) being "referred" to if the umpires could not agree.
The promotion of referees to the dominant position they occupy today, and the reformation of umpires into the linesmen role, occurred as part of a major restructuring of the laws in 1891.
The two assistant referees are instructed by the referee to each patrol half of a single touchline on opposite sides of the field.
